verdict.rationale: First-party docs show that registrable webhooks notify you of changes in workflow status, so results can arrive by webhook instead of polling. Each webhook is signed with an HMAC-SHA256 of the request body, keyed by the webhook's secret token. missing for 10: explicit enumeration of lifecycle event types (created, processing, verified, requires-input), independent or hands-on corroboration of delivery and signing behavior.

support.subject: As a developer, verification lifecycle events arrive as signed webhooks — created, processing, verified, requires-input — so my system reacts to outcomes without polling

citations.quote: asynchronously monitor the status of identity verification workflows by configuring webhook events to notify you of changes in workflow status
You can get the expected signature of the webhook by computing the HMAC of the event request body using the SHA256 algorithm, using the webhook's secret token as the key.
retrieve results via webhook or polling
